title: Cedar Home — Where is my order?
description: A fictional two-person order-status call. Maya Bennett is checking a delayed bedside lamp intended as a birthday gift. Ben Carter explains the courier status, delivery window and next steps. Target: about 90 seconds including short gaps. Both participants are prerecorded.

presenters.name: Maya Bennett
presenters.description: Customer · British woman in her early sixties. Thoughtful, courteous and capable; concerned about a birthday gift, then reassured.

presenters.name: Ben Carter
presenters.description: Customer service advisor · British man. Warm, confident and reassuring, with a measured conversational pace and clear explanations.

cues.speaker: BEN_CARTER
cues.text: Hello, thank you for calling Cedar Home customer service. You're speaking with Ben. How can I help today?

cues.speaker: ELAINE
cues.text: Hi, I ordered a bedside lamp on Monday. <sigh> It was due yesterday, but it hasn't arrived. It's a birthday present for tomorrow.
cues.deliveryDirection: British, female, age 61, calm/capable, thoughtful without sounding frail; clear articulation and natural pauses; avoid overacting grief. Mild concern about a delayed birthday gift. Keep the sigh soft and brief, without anger or theatrical exasperation.

cues.speaker: BEN_CARTER
cues.text: I'm sorry it's late. Could I have your name and order number, please?

cues.speaker: ELAINE
cues.text: Maya Bennett. <short pause> The order number is four eight one seven.

cues.speaker: BEN_CARTER
cues.text: Thanks, Maya. I'll check the latest delivery update for you.

scenes.title: The delivery update and a clear next step

cues.speaker: BEN_CARTER
cues.text: Your lamp was dispatched on Tuesday. <short pause> The courier had a delay, but it's out for delivery today.

cues.speaker: ELAINE
cues.text: <exhales> That's good. Do you know when it'll arrive?
cues.deliveryDirection: British, female, age 61, calm/capable, thoughtful without sounding frail; clear articulation and natural pauses; avoid overacting grief. Gently relieved by the delivery update. Use a small, relaxed exhale and keep the following question conversational.

cues.speaker: BEN_CARTER
cues.text: The delivery window is two to four this afternoon. Your confirmation email has a link to track it.

cues.speaker: ELAINE
cues.text: I've found it. Will that show me if the time changes?

cues.speaker: BEN_CARTER
cues.text: Yes, it shows the latest update. If your lamp hasn't arrived by four, call us and we'll check with the courier.

cues.speaker: ELAINE
cues.text: Perfect. <chuckle> I was worried it had gone missing. <short pause> Thanks for checking.
cues.deliveryDirection: British, female, age 61, calm/capable, thoughtful without sounding frail; clear articulation and natural pauses; avoid overacting grief. Warm and relieved. Use one quiet, brief, slightly self-conscious chuckle rather than broad laughter. Finish with sincere gratitude.

cues.speaker: BEN_CARTER
cues.text: You're welcome, Maya. I hope you enjoy the lamp. Goodbye.
